utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, The Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to all. May we begin in the usual manner by taking the appearances for today, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning. Tom Hannis with Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For Zupljanin, Igor Pantelic, Dragan Krgovic, and Ms. Katarina Danicic Case Manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While the usher is escorting the witness back to the stand, when we adjourned yesterday, Mr. Pantelic had asked for an additional 45 minutes. The Chamber rules that he has an additional 30 minutes to complete his cross-examination of Dr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Pantelic. And please given that we are here on the 27th of January, allow me to wish you, all members of the Defence team, and your clients a very happy day of Saint Sava.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your wishes. Yesterday when we adjourned we are discussed of the structure of CSB like in accordance with the rules and rule book. Would you agree with me if I put to you the proposition that Mr. Zupljanin in his capacity of chief of CSB was not in a narrow sense commander, but rather the co-ordinator who under his authority has several departments not only strictly related to the police issues, but and administrative, et cetera. So that we have to have a difference between the commander of the police and the chief of CSB, which is more administrative -- administrative and co-ordinative function?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And in CSB Banja Luka there were two sectors. Sector for national security and sector for public security commanded by -- and headed by, actually, the chiefs, respective chiefs. Would you agree with me if I put to you that chief of sector for public security was actually commander of the police units within the jurisdiction of CSB Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that at the operational control level on a day-to-day basis, command was within the jurisdiction of the public security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that also under the command of chief of sector for public security service were also Special Police units in this structure?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the Special Police units were at the CSB level. Obviously this changed, as we've discussed, after August 1992, but during the early period under public security which again was subordinate to the chief of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And speaking of the special unit of CSB Banja Luka, would you agree with me if I can tell you that several forms of this unit in accordance with the regulations were -- one of these is joint police unit which actually was combined of all active and reserve police forces within the area of competence of CSB Banja Luka, and the amount, the numbers were around 900?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were contingency plans, for example, in cases of riots and such, for reserve police forces and active police personnel to join in a larger force. However, I'm most familiar with a smaller unit of approximately, I think, 160 or 170 persons that was commonly known to be the Special Police unit of CSB Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is a third form of the units. And in between these two there is a third one, actually, which is manoeuvring unit of police which has a number around 700. Were you aware about this unit also which was in the structure of CSB?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that there were several different forms of the unit. The one that is visible most prominently in the documentation is the smaller unit to which I referred.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And speaking of this smaller unit were you aware or did you find when you were reviewing all these documents in your work that the commander of this unit was Mr. Mirko Lukic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Were you familiar with the fact that Mr. Lukic was active army officer at that time?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the status of Mr. Lukic. I know that he together with Ljuban Ecim were the two most prominent figures in the Special Police unit of CSB Banja Luka during the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But Mr. Lukic was in fact commander of that unit; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is sometimes the case that Mr. Lukic appears as the commander of the unit, that is correct. There are other periods during which, at least at an operational level, it appears from the documentation that it is Mr. Ecim who is conducting certain operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that the many chiefs of SJB which we know that these are local police organisations, many chiefs were not professionalists, but rather people and persons with the other education like machine engineers, jewelists, former police -- former army officer, even teachers. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that some chiefs of SJBs had professional backgrounds other than the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean comparing to the period before 1992, would you agree with me that a certain level of local political authorities were requested like nomination from local community or a procedure for, I don't know, elections, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to elections of police officials, or?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, appointment of police officials on the bases of the recommendation of the political structure of the local community. Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm certainly familiar with the fact that from the period from April a 1992 until the autumn of 1992, the Crisis Staffs in particular at the municipal level often interfered, nominated, proposed, or otherwise involved themselves in the selection of police personnel at the municipal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also you are aware of the fact that after the multi-party elections in Bosnia in 1993 [sic], ruling parties SDA, HDZ, and SDS were actually negotiating the candidates for each particular position including police, on various levels of course?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were involved at all levels, and as I noted previously, even before the war, this led to the appointments by all three parties, occasionally of people who were not professionals.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just correction to the transcript, page 5, line 6, instead of 1993 in my question, it was 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, were you aware of the fact that Mr. Zupljanin being elected -- appointed, actually, as chief of CSB Banja Luka after multi-party elections in 1990, actually was not member of SDS party?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that as far as I know, Mr. Zupljanin was not a member of the SDS party, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me and/or maybe are you familiar with the fact that the actual first candidate of SDS party for CSB Banja Luka was Mr. Vlado Tutus also an active police officer at that time? Just say yes or no, if you are familiar, okay, if not --

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And maybe you are familiar or not, but actually Muslim party SDA was against the nomination of Mr. Tutus at that time, and they gave permission only to the professional police officer without party affiliation which was Zupljanin. Did you come to the attention of this information?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the SDA's position on Mr. Zupljanin prior to 1992, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Nielsen, I would like to have your opinion with regard to the disciplinary and criminally responsibility -- criminal responsibility of the members of police forces. In your report you spoke about the rule book, about the regulations, laws, et cetera. I will put to you one situation, and I kindly ask you to give me an answer. If police officer committed a crime or a lesser offence like misdemeanour or something else, but I'm focused on the crime act, in performing his duty, what is the first duty of local chief of police, chief of SJB in accordance with the laws and regulations?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you discussing the period prior to the formation of the RS or the period of the RS?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Of the period of the RS.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, the primary responsibility of the local chief of police would be to initiate a disciplinary commission that would examine the charges against the officer in question, and from there the practice diverges depending on whether we are looking at a minor disciplinary infraction or a misdemeanour or a more serious criminal charge. Obviously if it's a more serious criminal charge, the matter is handed to the public prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then the relevant public prosecutor is in charge to give additional orders to police to collect certain evidence necessary for investigation or to obtain additional witness statements, et cetera. Would you agree with me that this is the process?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And chief of SJB was obliged to put this particular event in his daily report to the superior -- superior organ which is CSB; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that's correct, although I'm not aware that if it's a minor -- a very minor disciplinary infraction that it would warrant report. But certainly for more serious charges, it should be reported to the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And also this particular situation with the serious violation which is a criminal act actually committed by a police officer, this information would be also a part of weekly or monthly report from SJB to CSB; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reports about disciplinary and criminal procedures against active police officers and data pertaining to such reports should, according to the ministry's reporting regulations, be reported upwards from the SJB to the CSB and on to the ministerial level which is what results in the reports dianalytical reports that I mentioned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Nielsen, in preparation and process of work, your work to prepare this report, did you find any report from SJB to CSB where local chief of police was reporting that certain violation of rules or laws or commitment of crime was -- was actually a case taking place in this particular municipality?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of such documents, and I have viewed such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. As an example, I can mention reports, I believe it is from the municipality of what used to be called Bosanski Novi where they report that -- and also from Sanski Most where they report about alleged crimes that have been committed by active police officers, particularly the special unit to which we referred to before, and noted that the municipal civilian authorities are unhappy about the behaviour of such active police officers. I'm also aware of reports in other municipalities, sometimes they do not mention who the active police officers in question are, but mention in a general manner that in the context of looting or plundering abandoned houses that some uniform police officers are allegedly involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So my understanding from your answer is that actually there were very general, I would say, reports or, I don't know, informations, not specific for specific -- against the specific police officer who committed a specific crime; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always. There are cases, again specifically with reference to the CSB Banja Luka special unit where members of that unit who I know from the payroll and information about that unit were active members of that unit at that time are mentioned by name as allegedly having participated in criminal activities. And indeed as I state in my report, that actually led to the arrest of some of those members in the summer of 1992. They were later forcibly freed from the Banja Luka prison Tunjica by members of the CSB Special Police unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in a particular report from a local police chief, chief of SJB. Do you have in mind particular report from someone of chief of SJBs in mind? Can you tell me the name and the function?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe -- I don't know if I can remember his first name, but Mr. Vrucinic who was head of the SJB, if memory serves, I think in -- I can't remember whether it was Sanski Most or Kotor Varos. But certainly he was one of the chiefs of SJBs who filed such a report, and which I have reviewed in the course of preparing this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So among all municipalities, only chief of SJB Sanski Most Mr. Vrucinic filed this kind report; am I right? Based on your reviewing of documents?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that would be incorrect. I state that he was the one that I immediately recall. I also can recall examples of similar reports from, for example, Eastern Herzegovina, CSB Sarajevo area, and other municipalities in the CSB Banja Luka area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, please just listen. We are speaking about the region of CSB Banja Luka, so if I would be interested in the larger area, I will ask you. So to conclude, in your work, you came to the attention that in official capacity only chief of SJB Sanski Most filed a report against his police officers from his police unit in Sanski Most; am I right or not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You are again misstating my position. My position is that that is the example that immediately comes to mind, but I am aware of having reviewed other examples of such documentation from the operational area of CSB Banja Luka. There are not many, but there are more than that one. That is -- of that I'm absolutely sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And tell me in formation of police forces of all three nations in Bosnia, what were the insignia and coat of arms of, for example, Serbian police in 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: After April?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: After April.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that in the instructions that Mr. Zupljanin sent out in the beginning of April, he noted, I believe, that the insignia and coat of arms of the Serbian police should be the Serbian tricolour, the Trobojka, and that would be the badge identifying Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what was the case of Croatian police at that time?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that they used the "sahovnica," chequerboard of Herceg-Bosna, at least later in 1992. Again I'm not an expert on the Herceg-Bosna police, but I know that at some point in 1992, they systematically started to use the sahovnica as their emblem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about the members of Muslim police forces, what was the insignia and coat of arms of this police force?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know precisely what the date was, but after the independent Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina adopted its own regulations on insignia, I believe that they used the shield with the Lilies and the blue background which we are familiar with from the war time Bosnian flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me actually in this process of dissolution or separation of -- and speaking now of police forces, every member of police went to his, I would say, national group or entity in performing his future police works, many police officers moved from one territory to another territory for various reasons?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that for various reasons many police officers moved. I would not agree that every member of the police went to, as you put it, his national group or entity in performing his future police functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. But you would agree with me that very few Serbs police officers left in Muslim or Croat police forces in accordance with your knowledge? Maybe you know or you don't know.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the data that I have for the RS MUP, but I do know that the percentages of Serbs left in the Muslim or Croat police forces in Bosnia were quite modest, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. You were also aware of the rough number of around 600 police officers Serbs came from Croatia, because in 1991 there was clashes there, so they were fired, or for various reasons they came to Bosanska Krajina, are you aware of this fact?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I discussed that fact in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, could we have a document, please, it's 65 ter 279. And the page is of B/C/S version 6, and the English version is 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the meantime, Dr. Nielsen, you would agree with me, would you not, that chief of police in Prijedor, a Muslim, Talundzic was co-ordinating in more details activities with the SDA at the period of before the outbreak of the hostilities? Do you have this kind of information?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that allegations were made against Mr. Talundzic by Serbs that he was co-ordinating his activities with the SDA. I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Nielsen, please take a look on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, what do we have in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We have, Your Honour, document which was offered by Stanisic Defence. This is a report of MUP of Republika Srpska for of period April/December 1992. And this document was discussed with Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So I would like to draw your attention to the third paragraph where --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have a problem with English. Is that page 7 of English? Okay. Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So now this is -- in English version this is the last paragraph. Mr. Nielsen, you used this document in your report in terms of to support your claim that MUP of Republika Srpska was illegally organised; am I right? That was your position? Yes or no, just simple question.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not my position. That's the position of the RS MUP in its own document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Great. Now, you know the catch with the translation, with the spirit of language, et cetera. I put to you, Mr. Nielsen, that word in the second line of B/C/S paragraph 3, a word "ilegano" is not a proper translated in English with word "illegal" organisation. I put to you that the more proper wording in English would be a secret or undercover, not illegally, and I will give you a basis for that. Using a word which is not originated from Serbian language, "illegal" is something which is in use of in B/C/S language even from the time of Second World War for so-called movement of resistance, and the usual use of word "illegal" means -- is related to illegality or movement of resistance, et cetera. So the author of this document was not use this word in Serbian language which corresponds to the word of unlawful or illegal in English. Would you agree with this approach that I just explain?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's the most entertaining explanation of the word illegal I've ever heard. And I've been watching a lot of partisan movies lately, so I'm well familiar with traditionalists, but I don't agree with that interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, you cannot agree with that, that's your position. So, tell me, Mr. Nielsen, if the at that time Republika Srpska was established and constitution was adopted, that was a fact of public knowledge; am I right? I mean, nothing was hidden? Was the fact of establishment of Republika Srpska, adoption of constitution and laws, was it secret or public?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not a discussion about whether it's secret or public, it's a discussion about whether it was legal or illegal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, please, it's a very simple and straightforward question. Was the fact that Republika Srpska was established in January 1992 and adoption of constitution and all relevant laws, was that a fact of public knowledge, or Republika Srpska was organised in undercovered operations or in totally secret circumstances? Just give me answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That one fact was public knowledge. It also involved covert preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But, of course, if Republika Srpska was established with all its functions and organs, how Ministry of the Interior is considered illegal under these circumstances? Is it strange? How -- then, I mean, correct me if I'm wrong, then even Republika Srpska should be proclaimed illegal by its leadership? It's not logical, Mr. Nielsen, what you are saying to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object. That's about four questions. Secondly, this witness has been indicated several times by the Defence as not being an expert on legal matters or constitutional matters, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Nielsen, would you agree with me that in accordance with the general framework of constitutional principles in Bosnia during negotiation in Brussels, three entities were suggested to be a part of independent and sovereign state of Bosnia-Herzegovina; am I right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was part of the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And finally, the crown of this process of international negotiations and arrangements was Dayton Peace Accord with the two constituent units; am I right? I mean, this is a fact of common knowledge of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, I'm not sure what the crown of this process means, and the Dayton negotiations were after a long and protracted war. So I don't see that they were part of the Cutileiro negotiations that were going on in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I put to you, Mr. Nielsen, that on the basis of EU negotiations in 1992, the end of this process of international intervention and mediation was a Dayton Peace Accord where all relevant parties agreed to create a Bosnia-Herzegovina with two constituent units, do you agree with me or not?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with that assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Nielsen, in the paragraph 88 of your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, your 30 minutes having been exhausted, this is your final question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, in paragraph 88 of your report, you stated that by the end of March 1992 Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was clearly nearing dissolution. In light of these findings, I put to you that Republika Srpska and its respective government with its ministries including MUP is a constituent entity of Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that nothing was illegal when the ministry of internal affairs of Republika Srpska was established. Do you agree with my position or not? Yes or no yes, Mr. Nielsen.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree and point out again that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the MUP uses the word illegal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I don't have further question for this witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Before I start, there was a mention of Mr. Tutus as the chief of the -- or being proposed for the CSB position, and it reminded me, I think Judge Delvoie last week had a question for us when I think it was Mr. Krzic was testifying. And I think you indicated, Judge, that you didn't find him on your chart as chief --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I found him on the next page, not on the first -- the first page of the chart, there is no CSB -- SJB of Banja Luka mentioned, but on the second part, the next page there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to bring to your attention. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, I want to go back to last year and the beginning of the cross-examination on the 15th of December. Just a general matter, Mr. -- I don't recall if it was Mr. Zecevic or Cvijetic was asking you about your work in the leadership research team at the OTP. At page 4800, you were asked, When you say researching the leadership, you mean researches for the cases against Izetbegovic, Tudjman, Karadzic, Krajisnik, Milosevic? Are those the cases you mean? And you said, Yes. My question is, did the leadership go beyond those gentlemen and include other leaders such as top figures in the military and the police in those various republics of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work of the leadership research team focused on the civilian leaderships, police and political of all of the political entities operating in Yugoslavia from 1990 to 1999, and the primary military leadership research was conducted by the military analysis team.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to refer to the transcript at page 4836, there was a discussion with you by Defence counsel about Mr. Zepinic and the council of ministers. And I think it was Mr. Zecevic who said to you: "Mr. Nielsen, I'm quite certain I assert that Mr. Zepinic was in charge of the Ministry of the Interior and that Mr. Mico Stanisic was minister without portfolio in the ministerial council." And at line 22 you said: "I would again state that the context of the discussion that takes place about their respective appointments makes it very clear in my mind that because of the already then declining trust in Mr. Zepinic, Mr. Mico Stanisic was without portfolio but was, as it were, a shadow minister or a shadow councillor for Mr. Zepinic."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And to discuss this I'd like to look at P10. Exhibit P10. These are the minutes from the fourth session of the Assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia on the 21st of December 1991. And I think if we could start with page 35 in the English, and I think the B/C/S page in e-court is page 73.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on this first page you'll see that the list of proposed members for the council of ministers. You recall seeing that with Mr. Zepinic as number 3, and Mr. Stanisic not appearing in the initial list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall examining that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page in English. And the next page in B/C/S. Actually we need to go to one further page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll see the speaker is noted as Mr. Bjelosevic who is expressing his disagreement with the proposed appointment of Mr. Zepinic. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that discussion in the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And farther down on the English page we see the chairman. Who was the chairman at this session, by name, if you know?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the -- normally the chairman would have been Mr. Krajisnik, but I would have to look at the first page to make sure that he was indeed presiding at this session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And he indicates that there always be more than one proposal for particular position, and decisions on particular appointments will be made according to what we think is the best person to do the particular job. And the next speaker is Mr. Jovan Sarac, who supports the previous speaker and proposes appointing Mr. Mico Stanisic in the council of ministers in charge of these issues. Now, given where that appears in the minutes, what is he referring to when he says "in charge of these issues"? Referring to the matters for which Mr. Zepinic has been proposed?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding that, as I state in my report, because of a prevailing deep dissatisfaction in the SDS with the conduct of Mr. Zepinic on issues related to Serbs in the SRBiH MUP, a number of SDS politicians including Mr. Jovan Sarac are proposing Mr. Mico Stanisic to sit in the council of ministers, as it were, as a kind of shadow on Mr. Zepinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, if we can stay on this page in the English, but we need to go to page, I think, 77 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Just a little further down after Mr. Knezevic speaks, we see the Mr. Chairman is noted as thanking the previous speaker and adding that clarification is needed: "I think we explained at the session before last that the council ministers should be filled by ministers, deputy ministers, assistants of ministers or other officials of appropriate level. The idea is that the council of ministers should be a kind of executive body of the Serbian Assembly." And then in the next paragraph he says: "If you agree, I would like it to propose that we include Mr. Mico Stanisic as well." Is that consistent with your view that Mr. Stanisic is being proposed to deal with police issues in addition to Mr. Zepinic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go finally to the next page of the English. I think we have to go to page 78 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You see in the middle of the page of the English, the chairman is speaking, and you'll note in capital letters is it says: "The Assembly unanimously adopts the proposed list of ministers and the appointments of the chairman..." There's no further comment suggesting that anything different than what you've inferred from this that Mico Stanisic was being appointed to, in effect, supplement the appointment of Vidomir Zepinic for matters related to the Internal Affairs, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Next at page --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Hannis, but I don't think it's proper. This is misinterpretation of the document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's a matter for submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Explain yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the document is very explicit in this respect, and I think -- I think the report by the witness is also very explicit in this respect. There is no -- there is no supplemental position for Mr. Mico Stanisic. Mico Stanisic is a minister without the portfolio, and minister within the ministry council for Internal Affairs is Mr. Zepinic. That is the decision of the Assembly. Now it appears, as Mr. Hannis is alleging, is that Mr. Zepinic was never, in fact, the minister for Internal Affairs, but Mico Stanisic was instead appointed to that post, which is not the fact. And it doesn't come out from the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let's put that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree with Mr. Zecevic that Mico Stanisic was not appointed to the post of minister in the council of ministers for Internal Affairs. My position in my report and now on the stand is that even though Mico Stanisic was appointed minister without portfolio, the circumstances surrounding his appointment to minister without portfolio and is reflected in this discussion in the Assembly and in numerous other documents that I discuss from that period is that, in fact, he was there to shadow Mr. Zepinic, who was indeed appointed as the minister for Internal Affairs in the council of ministers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And how did that work out in practice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Based on the documentation that I've been able to review, in practice it means that Mr. Zepinic at a rapidly declining pace, or I would say rapidly increasing pace, rather, is removed from the inside discussions regarding decisions that the SDS wishes to see implemented in the police, and that Mr. Momcilo Mandic and Mr. Stanisic are increasingly involved instead of Mr. Zepinic. This culminates in April with Mr. Zepinic's resignation and Mr. Stanisic's appointment as the first minister of Internal Affairs of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn to transcript page 4839, again on the 15th of December. You were shown a document 1D119, we don't need to call it up. That was a 18 March document in which Mr. Mandic was voicing certain complaints about Mr. Zepinic. And you were asked the question: "Serbs evidently were having a major rift amongst themselves; isn't that correct? And you answered: "That is correct." My question is that in March of 1992 were you aware of any rift between Momcilo Mandic and Mico Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of a rift between those two individuals at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Were you aware of any rift between Mr. Stanisic, Mico, Momcilo Mandic on the one hand and Radovan Karadzic on the other? Any rift between them?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time in March 1992, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next matter is just, I think, an error in the transcript or perhaps just a misspoken word. At page 4841 of the transcript you were being asked about the barricades that were set up in Sarajevo in March. And at line 19 you are talking about Mrs. Plavsic: "I take it that she's probably referring to, among other things, her unhappiness with the news magazine "Slobodna Bosna" which I make reference to there articles on the barracks as published in around 12 March." I think you meant to say articles on the barricades, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. On March 16th you were being asked about Exhibit P424.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could bring that up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You recall this is a document that included a list of candidates for training as Special Forces in the Republic of Croatia MUP. I think it's dated the 8th of July, 1991. Had you seen this document before it was presented to you in your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I stated that I had not seen that document previously to the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I don't see in the document itself any indication of who paid for the training or whether or not these trainees were MUP reservists. Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated previously, my knowledge about the modalities of this training is very limited, so I do not know whether it was the MUP or the SDA that was paying for this training.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And it appears that the SDA is merely recommending candidates. Do you know who would make the final decision about whether or not these proposed candidates would be received for training in the MUP of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware who was exactly in charge of determining that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it appears in the transcript at page 4854 that it was pointed out that in the text it says this was, "in keeping with the joint agreement of authorised representatives of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the MUP of the Republic of Croatia." There's no indication that this was being done in secret or clandestinely.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again with the caveat that I'm not an expert on this particular issue, I would note that, as I have done previously, that I am aware that during the same time-period there was both this kind of training of Bosnian MUP employees in Croatia going on, as well as training of Bosnian Serb members of MUP in Belgrade going on. I'm not aware whether that was envisaged as a part of procedure or whether that represented an innovation, but I'm certainly aware given the documents that Defence presented that such practices were ongoing on several sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Related to that you mentioned that you had an LRT colleague who dealt with the Croatian MUP. Just as a matter of curiosity, who was that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had colleagues who both dealt with the Croatian MUP and the Bosnian MUP. The colleague who dealt with the Croatia MUP, I believe there were two of them, Chuck Sudetich and William Tomljanovich.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to now move to transcript page 4909. You were being asked generally about the Bosnian Serbs actions in late 1991 and early 1992 in moving toward creating their own state. And you agreed that Republika Srpska was formed on the 9th of January 1992, and then you were asked: "Wouldn't it be logical to expect that a republic that is established would establish its own organs?" And you said, "yes." And then you were asked: "If the representative of a people decide to create a state and adopt such a decision at the Assembly, then it can be assumed surely that such a state would need to function, too, would it not?" Your answer: "Yes, within the context of their own plans, it indeed does." But related to this issue that we've discussed about whether or not the creation of a separate RS MUP was in accordance with something referred to as the Sarajevo agreement or the Cutileiro plan or agreement or otherwise, I note that you've discussed Exhibit 1D135 which is the 11 February meeting of senior Serb staff in the joint MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, we discussed that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And in Exhibit 1D133, which is dated the 22nd of February, and 1D134, 18 March, which are statements of principles referred to as the Cutileiro plan, we see indications that this was a matter that was still being discussed, although the Serbs had already been making preparations before that date; right?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I state in my report, at the latest in September 1991 the Bosnian Serbs began contemplating the possibility of forming their own Ministry of Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One thing I want to address with you, relates it to the 31 March dispatch sent by Momcilo Mandic, which is Exhibit P353, and then Mr. -- Minister Delimustafic's related telefax which is Exhibit 1D136.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could bring up those side by side in the B/C/S, I want to bring something to your attention and ask you a couple of questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the transcript at page 4913 you were asked by, I think it was Mr. Zecevic, about the timing of the sending of these documents. And on the left side of the screen you'll see the dispatch from Mr. Mandic, and you note at the top the header line that we typically see on a fax seems to indicate that this was being sent to -- well, it's kind of hard to see on Mandic's, but it appears to be to Radio Sarajevo. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that Radio Sarajevo was the recipient.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the time of transmission is 1358. Do you see that in the upper left?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In the upper right corner, we see 002, and some kind of icon, it appears to be like a page. Would it be safe to assume that refers to this as a second page of some sort of fax transmission?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, looking at the two page numbers, 002 and then 003 on the document on the right-hand side, that would seem to confirm my earlier conjecture that the two were sent as part of one fax. At least potentially.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. And the one on the right, and in the first page of the telefax from Delimustafic, you see the time of transmission is 1359?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page of that exhibit, of 1D136.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You see the time of transmission on that next page is 1400, and the page number is 4, 004?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. And I note also from the ERN stamps that these are in consecutive order, which is to say that they were found as part of one document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And if counsel will take my word for it, the next two pages are page 5 and 6, and they are transmitted at 1401. That seems to suggest that both these documents were transmitted to the same time to Radio Sarajevo, some sort of public press announcement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have to object now. I mean, I was patient enough with -- all these questions were actually leading to speculation on the part of the witness, but I'm objecting at this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I suspect I understand the basis of your objection, but could you articulate it for the record, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, it is put to the witness basically to speculate whether this is one document which was sent in a consequence one after the other, or a part of one document. And it's also -- it's also put to the witness that the document is -- the document is a press release, which the witness doesn't know, and he can only speculate on that, that it's a press release. I mean, in my position that's calling for speculation, with all due respect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fair, Your Honour. I'll withdraw that question. But the reason that I'm going into this amount of detail on this is because at transcript page 4913, Mr. Zecevic says: "This means that between Momcilo Mandic's dispatch which is P353 and the reaction of the minister of the interior, Mr. Alija Delimustafic, there's only one minute difference." Somehow trying to suggest that the Delimustafic document might be a later fabrication or something made up, at least that's how I viewed it. That's why I thought it was necessary to go into this because I think it's a reasonable reading that these were sent out together to Radio Sarajevo because it's a hot news item.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, the other thing that occurred to me, Mr. Hannis, is that I'm sure that I'm not the only person who has had experience with the headers on faxes not being accurate. So how much you can build on this, I don't know -- I don't that initial purpose is served by going down this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take your point but the fact that these appear to be consecutive pages and they are one minute apart, it may not be the right time, but it's probably the right time vis-à-vis the relative sending of those individual pages, if you take my.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: To the extent that this is relevant when the Chamber comes to assess the evidence, it will be taken into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next, Mr. Nielsen, I want to move to your cross-examination on the 17th of December at transcript page 4929. You were being asked about document 1D137.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is a document from Stojan Zupljanin to subordinate SJBs, I believe, related to the dispatch we saw from Mr. Mandic. And we saw Mandic's dispatch was the dated the 31st of March. You'll see the dispatch from Mr. Zupljanin is dated 3 April. And in the addressees in the second line we see it's going to the SRBH MUP, and my English translation says minister and deputy. Who would that be at that time in the SRBH MUP, if you know?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if legally speaking Mr. Zepinic might still on paper have been the deputy minister as he was before the 1st of April; but if it was not he, I don't know who it would have been on that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this question, the first line appears to be the Serbian Republic of BH Ministry; correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And SR, is that also the Serbian republic or is that the socialist republic of BiH?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, given -- there is a confusion during this period with the acronym SR because it can both mean Serbian republic or socialist republic, both in English and in B/C/S. But in this case it's clearly spelled out in the first line of the recipients, the Serbian republic of BiH, therefore I infer that in the second line when they refer to the SRBiH, they are not sending it twice to the same minister, they are sending it once to the minister of the Serbian republic and once to the minister of socialist republic and his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Moving to transcript page 4945, you were being asked about Mico Stanisic's appointment to the SRBiH MUP. I think on the 14th of February 1992, we were shown Exhibit 1D139 which was a decision by Delimustafic appointing Mico Stanisic as an advisor. When Mico Stanisic who was then a member of the joint MUP was appointed the minister of interior for the newly created Serb MUP, would he have taken an oath to become the minister of the Serb MUP, do you know?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to admit that I'm not aware whether ministers were required to take an official oath to the government of which -- to the government of which they were members.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you ever come across any document indicating that Mr. Mico Stanisic resigned from the BiH MUP or the joint MUP at or shortly after the time he became minister of the newly created Serb MUP?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen a document that indicates that an official resignation took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Now, on the 17th of December --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: On the 17th of December, Mr. Cvijetic was asking you some questions at page 4992. He was asking you about I think the law on the ministries -- or the law on state administration, I'm sorry. But that's one that we don't have an English version for.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, once we have an English translation I'd like to request an opportunity to perhaps come back to that issue, but I'm somewhat hamstrung not having any English to work with, so I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let's go to the 1982 Law on the All People's Defence. You were asked some questions about this by Mr. Cvijetic, and he addressed the portion of your report where you say: "In situations of immediate threat of war and other contingencies, the police may also be used to carry out combat task of the armed forces in keeping with law. During its engagement for combat activities in the armed forces, the police shall be under the command of the authorised officer in charge of the combat activity." And you said that you agreed with that principle as it was written in the Law on All People's Defence. And at page 5429, Mr. Cvijetic said to you: "Mr. Nielsen, according to military regulations in the system of All People's Defence all subjects in the state are duty-bound to prepare for All People's Defence, to make plans, to form staffs, and to take all other necessary steps." At the time the 1982 Law on All People's Defence was written, it's correct, isn't it, that the former Republic of Yugoslavia consisted of Serbs, Croats, Muslims, Romas, a variety of other peoples?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia contained a large number of nations and nationalities as they were called.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is it your understanding that in April, May, June, 1992, the Republika Srpska, as it came to be called, was following the 1982 Law on People's Defence because they had not yet formulated a new law?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all cases where the RS had not yet formulated its own law, they appeared to have been guided by the previously existing Yugoslav legislation. I am aware, and I do not at the present moment recall the exact date, but I am aware that in the course of 1992 they promulgated their own law on these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Which was different from the old ones, or were they just copies of the old ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them were to a large extent copies as indeed was the law on Internal Affairs, but certain passages were most certainly changed and updated. But I'm not an expert on the differences, and I have not compared the two laws on National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Speaking in general terms in 1992 after April in the Republika Srpska as part of All People's Defence, were Muslims and Croats being provided arms and invited to make plans and take part in the All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that open invitation to that effect was issued. That having been said, I am aware that both the RS MUP, as we've previously discussed, and the VRS contained very small percentages of non-Serbs who did serve on behalf of that republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And generally speaking, weren't weapons being removed from Muslims and Croats in the Republika Srpska by the army and the police?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is amply reflected in the police documentation that I have been able to examine, and I am aware that it's also amply reflected even more in the military documentation which my colleague Ewan Brown has examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At page 5430 and -31, then you were asked about Exhibit 1D46. Which is a document dated the 15th of May, 1992, an order issued by Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could have that up on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You are familiar with this one. This is the order basically creating or organising parts of the MUP into war units.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 2 in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In item 7 the last paragraph says: "While participating in combat operations, the units of the ministry shall be subordinated to the command of the arms forces. However, the ministry units shall be under the direct command of certain ministry officials." What is your understanding of that term "direct command of certain ministry officials"?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of that, and, indeed, as I understand it, the understanding of my esteemed colleague Mr. Bajagic whom I met in December and had read his report in the Borovcanin case, is that what this means in the operational level is that when a police unit is resubordinated to military command, it is under military command pursuant to the Law on National Defence as Mr. Cvijetic very correctly also stated, but that orders to the actual members of that police unit in the area, and so on, of combat activities are issued through the commanding officer of that police unit. So if the ranking police officer in the case of a combat activity is the commander of a Special Police unit, the chief of the military or the commander of the military activities on the VRS side would not simply go to any -- just any member of the police and say, Do this, or do that. He would first go to the commanding police officer and say, I order that your unit, for example, support the right flank of our offensive. This is to ensure that the police were not ordered to do things that their own commander was not aware of in the zone of combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this an appropriate time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. But before we go to the break, I was intrigued by some of the propositions made by counsel Pantelic when he was cross-examining the witness, because in Mr. Pantelic's cross-examination I gathered as much as the proposition that in the CSB of Banja Luka there were a number of different units, and I was left with a very unclear impression of if these units really existed, and how many officers were in them, and what was their function. And I really don't know if indeed this is relevant information to the Chamber, but just in order to take advantage of the presence of the expert witness, I would propose to Mr. Pantelic, if you would be so good to offer a diagram of the structure of the CSB in Banja Luka, and maybe you could use the break to consult with your client about how the Banja Luka CSB was really structured. And if that's possible, we can then after the break put it to the witness, and of course, Mr. Hannis will be given an extra chance to comment on that. But I -- it may not be relevant, but yet it may, actually. So let's use the existence and presence of the expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have a diagram for Banja Luka CSB yet. I know we are working to see if we can provide one to the Court. I don't know if Mr. Pantelic has anything for you or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The idea was, I think, that you should finish your re-examination and then at some time, Mr. Pantelic may or may not put a draft diagram on the ELMO, and we'll hear the witness whether he has any comments to it, and you will then be allowed to put further questions in relation to the comments made by the witness, and then we'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. I anticipate finishing well before the end of the day, and I would indicate to the Court that our next witness won't be available to start until tomorrow. So if we finish early maybe we can look at the Banja Luka diagram and address some other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Nielsen, we were looking at 1D46, the 15 May order from Minister Mico Stanisic. I had a question for you. Item 7 talks about the use of the ministry units in co-ordinated actions with the armed forces of the Serbian Republic of BH may be ordered by the minister. We already looked at the last paragraph under number 7 about "while participating in combat operations." Do you read co-ordinated action in -- I see Mr. Zecevic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I was wondering if we could have this document on the e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't notice they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And before we see it in e-court, Your Honours, with your permission, I think that the starting question of my learned friend was, "do you read co-ordinated action in," I think it's slightly leading, so I'm not reading a mind of my learned friend, but I think we have to get an opinion, expert opinion on the issue from Mr. Nielsen. Maybe I'm wrong, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Sorry, where is this question, Mr. Pantelic? I am looking at the transcript. Where will I find the question to which you are taking objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: The ongoing question, actually, of my learned friend, so let's hear and then we can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I hadn't finished my question, so I think the objection is a bit premature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In item 7, you see the first sentence says, The use of the ministry units in co-ordinated action. In the third paragraph in item 7 you see a reference to combat operations. What is your understanding of the term co-ordinated action in the first line? Do you read that to include something beyond combat operations or exclusively combat operations?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first line of point 7 of this document just uses the rather vague term co-ordinated actions, or co-ordinated action as it's translated in English. I think it's clear that this document -- the ambit of this document is to discuss joint activities of the VRS and the RS MUP, in particular combat activities. But it's obviously the case that in operations outside combat activities, for example, the apprehension of paramilitary groups in Zvornik at the end of July 1992, that was a joint military police operation; that was not a combat activity. So it was not only in combat that the MUP and the VRS would cooperate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And that first paragraph says that the use of the ministry units may be ordered. Does that raise an inference that the MUP may decline to order MUP units to participate in any particular co-ordinated actions?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there's two points to be made here. One is that it appears that the minister in point 7 may himself order certain joint activities to take place that involve both the VRS and the RS MUP, and again these joint activities do not necessarily need to mean joint combat activities. The other point that I think needs making at this stage is that it is evident, as I have testified previously, that on a number of occasions, the minister of Internal Affairs demonstrated his annoyance at the use of police units for combat activities without proper notification to him as minister. And this order, a large point of this order, is to ensure that the VRS does not go and use one resubordinated unit for one particular combat activity, and then without consulting back to the ministry, go on to use them for a whole bunch of other activities. There is an agreement ongoing, and it's discussed and reflected in the government minutes in the summer of 1992, that the police is supposed to be used for discreet activities when it's resubordinated to the VRS. And if the VRS then decides that it still needs the services of the MUP, it's supposed to go back to the minister of Internal Affairs and say look, can you agree that we continue to use the MUP for such activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What do you mean by discreet operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, whether it's tasks or operations, there is -- the VRS commander would say, I need to use MUP forces because we need reinforcements on the front, because we need to arrest looters, we need to round up military conscripts, whatever the purpose of that activity may be. And the minister says, Yes, I agree, you can have this unit, and these particular units of the police are resubordinated to you. Now, if he then find out six weeks later that the military command in that area is still ordering around the police and using them for all kind of other things that minister did not originally -- and the relevant police officials did not originally grant permission for, then that would be perceived by the MUP as a breaking of that agreement. I note that this takes place in the context as is evident in all the RS MUP documentation that the minister of Internal Affairs wants the police to get back to being police and get them out of combat. There's a great quote from the ministry in the report where he says, I do not want to see a situation in which the police is conducting -- or, excuse me, the military is conducting traffic while the police are in the trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Just briefly, if you can, Mr. Nielsen, how were these conflicts between the MUP and the army resolved in practice? Is there any pattern in the way in which these issues were resolved, or was it just the minister of interior barking at the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I note in the brief section of my report on the co-operation of RS MUP with the VRS, there were ongoing negotiations, a Planum that was set up under the supervision of the Presidency in which the minister of Internal Affairs and Ratko Mladic and other military commanders were supposed to be meeting and agreeing continuously that whenever there were conflicts they would try to ease them through such negotiations and resolve them on an ad hoc basis. It's overall the case, as is reflected in the RS MUP annual report and the minister's interview in October 1992 that until the end of 1992 the level to which the police was of involved in combat activities far exceeded that which the ministry itself wished to see. But I do note, and I state in my report, quoting Mr. Mico Stanisic's interview in October 1992, that is in paragraphs 392 to 395 of my report, that Mico Stanisic said that overall he was satisfied with the co-operation with the VRS in the course of 1992, and he played down any notion of conflict of responsibilities between the two organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Dr. Nielsen, in paragraph 8 it talks about "... in military operations military regulations and rules shall be enforced." If you could look at the original and in paragraph 7 you see the reference to co-ordinated action and also to combat operations. Here in paragraph 8 we see military operations. Are those three distinct terms that are used in the original?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm immediately seeing two key terms, one is "sadejstvo" in B/C/S, which is translated merely as co-ordinated action. The other is "borbena dejstva" which is combat activities. And the key distinction here, as we have discussed previously, is that if the -- if an employee of the RS MUP commits, for example, crimes during the period in which is he resubordinated to the VRS and participating in joint combat activities, then point 8 states that it is military regulations and rules that shall be enforced. If on the other hand, he is carrying out duties which are pursuant to his job under the law in internal affairs, then it is the relative -- with the police regulations on disciplinary responsibility that apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you clarify for me whether the term combat operations in paragraph 3 of item number 7 is the same phrase in B/C/S as what is translated in paragraph 8 or item 8 paragraph 1 "military operations"?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct. There are two terms being used. One is "borbena dejstva" which is combat activities, and one is "vojna dejstva" which is military activities. As far as I know and not being a military expert, these two are, for all intents and purposes, synonyms.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me go next to take a look again at Exhibit P427.14 that you were shown on Monday at transcript page 5443. This is a 28 May 1992 document from Major Andric to the Zvornik TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You looked at that before. I want to ask you about item number 6 which says: "The moving out of the Muslim population must be organised and co-ordinated with the municipalities through which the moving is carried out. Only women and children can move out, while men fit for military service are to be placed in camps for exchange." It's not clear from this document whether the men in the Muslim population are captured fighters or old male civilians living at home. Did you see other documents reflecting that non-Serb males, non-combatants were being detained or held for purposes of exchange.

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that, and that is reflected in paragraphs, I believe, 3 -- excuse me, 298 through approximately 302 of my report. I note that there was a discussion about detained persons of Muslim and Croat ethnicity in which they ultimately, as I state in paragraph 298, devised, and this is reflected in a letter written by Mr. Zupljanin on the 20th of July to Mr. Mico Stanisic, to the sorting of detained individuals into three categories. The first was comprised of persons suspected of commission of criminal acts. The second was comprised of persons suspected of aiding and abetting those in the first category. And the third was comprised, and I quote from the document: "Of adult males concerning whom the service has not to date gathered any security relevant data on the bases of which these persons may be treated as hostages." And there is an internal discussion in the ministry where Tomislav Kovac and Stojan Zupljanin and Mico Stanisic are involved as to what to do with these individuals. Zupljanin proposed the exchange of military-aged males in the afore mentioned third category for Serbs being held under similar circumstances by the Muslim Croat forces. The concern at this time that is reflected in many documents is that if the Muslim military-aged males were allowed to move out, as this document phrases it that we have in front of us, they would return from their refugee locations and rejoin the struggle against the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In your report you indicate that this was a subject matter of discussion at meetings of the high-level members of the RS MUP, and I think you've pointed to various documents reflecting an awareness of this problem of non-Serb civilians being held without any kind of charges being filed. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And again, the paragraphs which I previously mentioned reflect some of the correspondence that relates to that discussion at the level of the CSB and at the level of the ministry. And it was also discussed at government sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You were shown by Defence counsel some documents reflecting Minister Mico Stanisic's directions to subordinates to treat detained individuals in accordance with the Geneva Conventions and humanitarian law principles. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall being shown documents by Radovan Karadzic to that effect, and them having been forwarded by Mr. Stanisic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you find in your review of the documents anything showing direct action taken by Minister Stanisic or the MUP with regard to this category of persons such as releasing these people forthwith, or refusing to continue to furnish police personnel to guard people held or detained in such capacity? Did you see anything like that?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated previously, in August 1992 and from -- actually from mid-July 1992 Minister Stanisic was pressuring his subordinates to divest RS MUP of responsibility for detention facilities as quickly as possible. In practice, what this meant is that in the course of August 1992 in particular, the police did indeed for the most part cease to operate and guard detention facilities. And those persons detained at facilities such as Omarska, Keraterm, and Trnopolje were sent to Manjaca, the military detention facility, where the military was then in charge of their further fates. I do note and it is the case, and I state it in paragraph 311 of my report, that Mr. Stanisic in his capacity as minister issued orders that all RS MUP personnel dealing with detainees obey the relevant domestic and international laws. That was a dispatch he issued in mid-August. I would also note, and it is reflected in my report, that the VRS complained particularly in the case of Prijedor municipality that they were receiving at Manjaca persons who had been detained at facilities under the control of the RS MUP for whom no accompanying documentation was given about the reasons for their detention. And in several cases, VRS officers filed reports to their superior officers noting the extremely poor physical state of these detainees, and in a few cases also the fact that they appeared to have been beaten and killed by the RS MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. You were shown at page 5449 on Monday a document that has identification number 1D03-0496.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could have that up in e-court, please. And the English is 1D03-0498.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is a document that apparently has a handwritten date on it of 9 December 1992 from Colonel Tolimir relating to prisoners still in Manjaca POW camp. You recall looking at that yesterday or Monday?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page in the English, and it's the fourth paragraph in the B/C/S, it makes reference to: "With respect to the Muslims for whom you have operational and technical documentation..." And later on in the paragraph it says, "and against whom you have not submitted criminal reports do so immediately." Do you have any idea how long some of these prisoners would have been held as of December 1992? Or do you have any way of knowing?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know from the relevant police documentation that some individuals were detained for a period that certainly extended over a period of several months, but I'm not aware of the specific lengths of detention of specific individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And were you aware that exchanges were still taking place in December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that fact, and I'm aware of the fact that there was an RS exchange commission established for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, that document was discussed with the witness yesterday, but it wasn't tendered by the Defence. I would like to tender it, just to put his testimony about it in context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P872, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Next if we could look at Exhibit P194. And if we could look at the last page in both the B/C/S and English versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'll tell you, Dr. Nielsen, this is the 17 August 1992 report of the commission on the inspection of collection centres and other facilities for captives in the Autonomous Region of Krajina. You are familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I discuss this document starting in paragraph 304 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we can look at the very last item number 6, in my English translation it reads: "The Ministry of Defence and the Ministry of the Interior should jointly prepare adequate regulations on the treatment of captives held in collection or investigation centres, or other facilities for accommodating these people." Did you find in your review of documents any definition of the term "collection centre" or "investigation centre"?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's, as with many terms used in the summer of 1992 in the RS, Crisis Staffs, War Presidencies, detention facilities, collection centres, there is a sloppiness with the use of terms, often they are undefined. And when reading the documents as an analyst, it appears that several terms are used to mean the same thing, yet at some times there seem to be subtle differences. So the terms "collection centre" and "investigation centre" are symptomatic of this. In the most narrow sense of the word, collection centre would mean a place where people are simply put and collected, whereas an investigation centre would be a place where people who are formally under investigation would be held and where judicial or police officials would come to investigate them. In practice, these things occur at both types of facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what about the term "other facilities" for accommodating these people? Any idea of what that is and how it differs from a collection or an investigation centre?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speculate that that might include reference to other buildings locations in which persons so defined were kept. I mean, there were a lot of improvised buildings and facilities that were operating for these purposes during the summer of 1992 and as of the writing of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether or not a prisoner of war camp would be included within these three terms, or is that something separate and apart, if you know?

utterances.speaker: CHRISTIAN NIELSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, there is a sloppiness in the original documentation with respect to the use of the term "prisoners of war." I would note that prisoners of war as defined by the RS officials were most certainly detained in military facilities.
